subsystems.name: Laser launch array
subsystems.role: accelerates the sail from the ground with a phased, coherent beam.
parts: many fibre or solid-state laser amplifiers

subsystems.name: Lightsail
subsystems.role: reflects the laser beam to produce thrust; must survive intense light and interstellar dust.

subsystems.name: StarChip probe
subsystems.role: the gram-scale payload that coasts to the target and takes measurements.

subsystems.name: Communication link
subsystems.role: sends data back across light-years with a tiny transmitter.

subsystems.name: Attitude and navigation
subsystems.role: keeps the sail pointed and the probe on course.
parts: sail shape control or movable mass

subsystems.name: Ground infrastructure
subsystems.role: powers, cools and aims the launch array and receives the return signal.

buildSteps.title: Make the sail
buildSteps.detail: Deposit an ultrathin reflective film on a sacrificial substrate, pattern it into a metre-scale sheet, and mount it on a lightweight frame. Test it under a high-power laser in vacuum to see if it survives.

buildSteps.title: Build the StarChip
buildSteps.detail: Integrate a camera, processor, power source and tiny laser transmitter onto a wafer-scale chip, then attach it to the sail.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the laser array
buildSteps.detail: Combine thousands of phase-locked laser amplifiers into one beam, with adaptive optics to correct atmospheric distortion.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Launch a small sail and push it with a ground laser to validate acceleration, pointing and sail stability.

buildSteps.title: Scale up the launch system
buildSteps.detail: Build a full array capable of delivering tens of gigawatts for several minutes, with power and cooling infrastructure.

buildSteps.title: Launch the probe fleet
buildSteps.detail: Place hundreds of sails in a high-altitude orbit, then release and accelerate them one by one.

buildSteps.title: Cruise and flyby
buildSteps.detail: After a few minutes of laser push, the probes coast for about 20 years to the target, then take images and spectra during a fast flyby.

buildSteps.title: Return the data
buildSteps.detail: Each probe points its transmitter at Earth; large telescopes receive the faint signal about four years later.

prerequisites.why: must reflect most light while absorbing little heat; only small laboratory sails have been tested.
laboratory and military lasers exist, but not a coherent array of the required power and duration.

prerequisites.tech: Gram-scale spacecraft with integrated power and communication
prerequisites.why: no flight-ready chip combines camera, processor and interstellar transmitter at that mass.
existing giant telescopes could detect a strong laser, but a dedicated array would be needed for reliability.
at a fraction of light speed, even tiny dust grains can destroy the sail or probe.
the sail must be aimed to within a tiny fraction of a degree over light-years.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations of laser-driven sails and solar-sail flights such as LightSail 2
pathway.unlocks: proof that thin sails can deploy and be pushed in space.

pathway.milestone: in-space laser sail acceleration tests over kilometres
pathway.unlocks: data on beam pointing, sail survival and controllability.

pathway.milestone: a full-scale laser array and a gram-scale probe design
pathway.unlocks: a credible precursor mission to the nearest stars.

pathway.milestone: launch of a fleet to Alpha Centauri and reception of flyby data
pathway.unlocks: first direct images of another planetary system.

pathway.milestone: relay or deceleration concepts for heavier payloads
pathway.unlocks: orbital reconnaissance rather than a fast flyby.
